title: Easter Monday, 2025
hookLine: Francis dies on Easter Monday, the day after blessing the crowd at Easter
last: WE ARE IN THE SAME BOAT.

lines: A FULL SQUARE ON EASTER SUNDAY.
A FRAIL BLESSING FROM THE BALCONY.
cards: Easter Sunday in Rome, and the square is packed. Flags, umbrellas, phones held high. On the balcony of Saint Peter's, a frail man in a wheelchair is brought out, his voice thin after a long illness.
He wishes the crowd a happy Easter, and someone beside him reads his Easter message aloud, because he can't.
Then, instead of going back inside to rest, he rides down into the square in the open car, slowly, blessing children held up to him. The next morning, Easter Monday, Pope Francis died.

teach.b: For some families, Easter Monday is a leftover day. In Italy it even has a nickname, Pasquetta, little Easter: picnics and the last of the chocolate.
But in the Church's calendar, Easter Monday is not simply the day after Easter. It is still Easter.

teach.h: AN OCTAVE: EIGHT DAYS KEPT AS ONE.
teach.b: The Church's norms for the liturgical year say the first eight days of the Easter season make up the octave of Easter, each one celebrated as a solemnity of the Lord. At Mass that Monday the alleluias still ring.

teach.h: A DEATH INSIDE THE EASTER SEASON.
teach.b: Easter, in effect, is too large for a single sunrise. So Catholics heard the news inside that long day: a man who had just blessed the city and the world died while the Church was still singing about the resurrection.

One of the Gospel readings the Church offers for funerals is Jesus speaking to Martha, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live."
That promise is offered at the funeral of anyone who dies in the faith, well-known or not. Francis seems to have wanted his own burial just as ordinary.

He asked to be buried simply, outside the Vatican, in the Roman basilica of Saint Mary Major, where he used to pray before and after his journeys, under a plain stone carrying only his name in Latin: Franciscus.

teach.h: I AM THE RESURRECTION AND THE LIFE.
teach.b: For the world outside, Easter Monday is a holiday in some places and a workday in others. For the Church it is still Easter morning.

how: Catholics keep the eight days from Easter Sunday as the octave of Easter, celebrating each day at Mass as Easter itself, and when a pope dies they pray for him at Masses offered for the repose of his soul.

games.q: you're Francis, weak after a long illness. it's Easter Sunday and the square below is full. you've given the blessing. what do you do?
o: ride down through the crowd in the open car.
send a cardinal out in your place.
games.why: he rode slowly through the square, blessing children held up to him. he died the next morning, Easter Monday.

practice: Say the names of popes who have died, the ones from these lessons or from your own lifetime: Francis, Benedict, John Paul, whoever comes, slowly, one at a time.
The Church's old prayer for the dead asks God to grant them eternal rest and to let perpetual light shine on them. If you pray, say it after each name; if you don't, give each name one quiet breath.

wordCard.voice: Easter Monday. The day after Easter Sunday, which the Church's calendar still keeps as Easter, inside the octave. The day Pope Francis died.
